sections.html:
North Las Vegas is a suburban city in Clark County, northeast of Las Vegas in the Mojave Desert. The population was 262,527 in the 2020 census, and the city is the fourth largest in Nevada. Homes range from older lots near the original townsite, known locally as Old Town, to recent subdivision houses in master-planned communities such as Aliante and Eldorado.

That mix means condition and age vary a lot from street to street. A cash buyer looks at each house as it stands, so you can sell without sorting out which repairs a lender would insist on.

sections.h2: What the desert climate does to a house
sections.html:
Heat is the main stress on a North Las Vegas home. July highs average about 105 degrees, and yearly precipitation is only about 4.6 inches. Nights in winter can fall below freezing, and summer monsoon storms bring heavy rain now and then.

Buyers and inspectors tend to look at the same few things:

  • The age and condition of the air conditioning system, which runs most of the year
  • Roof membranes and tile, which sit in direct sun for months
  • Block walls and fences, which the city treats as a code concern when they are damaged

You do not have to fix any of this to sell for cash. You do have to tell the buyer about defects you know of.

sections.h2: City rules that can slow a sale
sections.html:
Open code enforcement cases and short-term rental permits are the two city rules that most often complicate a sale. The city handles both, not Clark County.

The Code Enforcement Division focuses on these problems:

  • Boarding and securing vacant structures
  • Junk, litter, garbage and overgrown weeds
  • Junk vehicles and illegally posted signs
  • Illegal home businesses
  • Blocked streets or sidewalks and damaged fences or block walls

The division tries for voluntary compliance through notices and education. If that fails, it can abate the nuisance or issue criminal citations, and the city has an appeal and hearing process. Clear any open case before closing, or tell the buyer about it.

Short-term rentals face a higher bar. Ordinance 3127, adopted in June 2022, requires a Conditional Use Permit before a business license application. The application needs a notarized letter from the homeowners association, a 660-foot separation from other short-term rentals and a 2,500-foot separation from resort hotels. Planning and Zoning takes questions at (702) 633-1537.

sections.h2: What Nevada requires from a seller
sections.html:
The seller must complete a disclosure form at least 10 days before the property is conveyed, and cash sales are not exempt. Under NRS 113.130 the seller fills it out, and either the seller or the agent serves it on the buyer or the buyer's agent. An agent cannot complete it for you. If you later find a new defect, or a listed one gets worse, tell the buyer in writing before closing.

The statute lists exceptions: foreclosure sales, sales between co-owners, spouses or close relatives, the first sale of a house built by a licensed contractor, and certain fiduciary sales by a personal representative or trustee. A buyer cannot waive the requirement.

In Clark County the real property transfer tax is $2.55 per $500 of value. That is the statewide $1.95 plus a $0.60 county add-on. The County Recorder collects it when the deed is recorded. Buyer and seller are responsible together and individually, so the purchase contract should say who pays. Exemptions under NRS 375.090 include a transfer between former spouses under a divorce decree and a deed that takes effect on death.

If the house is in a homeowners association, you must furnish a resale package under NRS 116.4109. It holds the governing documents, a statement of unpaid assessments and fines, and the budget. The buyer can cancel until midnight of the fifth calendar day after receiving it.

The Clark County Treasurer bills real property tax once a year. A bill over $100 can be paid in four installments, and they are not quarterly.

Clark County installment schedule
InstallmentDue date
FirstThird Monday in August
SecondFirst Monday in October
ThirdFirst Monday in January
FourthFirst Monday in March

A payment must arrive within 10 days of the due date to avoid a penalty, which is 4 percent of the installment for one late payment. Unpaid taxes at the end of April are advertised as delinquent. If the amount is still owed on the first Monday in June, the county holds the property through a two-year redemption period, with interest at 10 percent a year.

If you are behind, ask the Treasurer for a payoff figure early. The office is at 500 S Grand Central Pkwy, phone (702) 455-4323, open Monday through Thursday.

A cash sale swaps the lender for the buyer's own funds, which removes loan approval and most of the appraisal delay. The Nevada requirements still apply: the disclosure form, the recorded deed, the transfer tax and any association paperwork. The usual order looks like this:

  1. You send the address and condition of the house and receive a written offer.
  2. A title company opens escrow and searches for liens, unpaid taxes and judgments.
  3. You complete the Nevada seller's disclosure and any HOA package.
  4. The deed is signed and recorded with the Clark County Recorder along with a Declaration of Value.
  5. Payoffs and fees come out of proceeds and you receive the balance.

We buy North Las Vegas houses as-is. Tell us about tenants, liens or unfinished repairs up front so the offer reflects them and the closing has no surprises.

faqs.q: Do I have to disclose problems if I sell my North Las Vegas house for cash?
faqs.a: Yes. NRS 113.130 requires the disclosure form at least 10 days before the property is conveyed, and cash sales are not among the exceptions. You only disclose defects you know about, and you must update the buyer in writing if you learn of a new one before closing.

faqs.q: How much is the transfer tax on a North Las Vegas sale?
faqs.a: In Clark County the rate is $2.55 per $500 of value, which is $1.95 statewide plus $0.60 for the county. The County Recorder collects it when the deed is recorded, and the contract decides who pays.

faqs.q: Can a North Las Vegas buyer turn my house into a short-term rental?
faqs.a: Only with a Conditional Use Permit from the city, which must come before a business license. The application needs a 660-foot separation from other short-term rentals, a 2,500-foot separation from resort hotels and a notarized HOA letter where one applies.

faqs.q: What happens if code enforcement has an open case on my house?
faqs.a: Code Enforcement can abate a nuisance or issue citations when notices are ignored, and you can appeal through the city. Resolve the case before closing where you can, and tell the buyer about anything still open.

faqs.q: When are Clark County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The third Monday in August. A bill over $100 can be paid in installments on that day and the first Mondays in October, January and March. A late payment starts at a 4 percent penalty.
